description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value: After dealing with the initial challenges posed by the pandemic, the training team re-designed the training trajectory to be done virtually through a series of one-day virtual training sessions with post-training assignments in between. Thus far, we have completed three e-workshops and the participants have completed three assignments to apply what they learned in the workshops. The participants were given additional resources related to the topics covered in the workshops. In addition to workshop reports, short videos on all three workshops were made, also for use as examples of participatory training in their work. The farmer innovations documented by the participants as one of their training assignments will be included in the catalogue of local innovation that will be produced by the end of the project in 2022.

All the planned activities were carried out with great success and indicators achieved beyond expectations: three training courses, post-training assignments, a study trip, the setting up of a multi-actor platform, two joint learning experiments, a food fair, two feedback workshops at ATVET level, a closing workshop, the production and printing of a catalogue of local innovations and extensive communication (print media, online media, Prolinnova website, audio-visual media, agricultural and innovation magazine, feedback video and summary documentary film).

comment.narrative: 24-01-2023: 3 public structures were initially involved in the implementation of the training program, including ATVET of Ina, ATVET of Kika and the University of Parakou. In addition, the establishment of a multi-actor platform for the promotion of local innovation and participatory innovation development included a total of 30 structures, 4 of which were public (including the 3 initial public structures of the program) and 26 private structures (NGOs and farmers' associations) | 23-04-2021: The staff of three educational institutions are being strengthened through this TMT+. They are the University of Parakou, the ATVET college Kika (Lycée Technique Agricole de Kika) and the ATVET college Ina (Lycée Technique Agricole d’Ina).

24-01-2023: All the 30 structures that make up the Prolinnova-Benin platform set up by the program have been strengthened, including 04 from public sector and 26 from private and civil society sector.
